title: Börek
subtitle: Turkish filo pastry rolls with feta and spinach
excerpt: Crisp rolled filo pastry filled with spinach and white cheese, brushed with egg and baked until shatteringly golden. The Turkish filo pie family, eaten for breakfast, lunch, and as a snack throughout Turkey and the Balkans.

recipe.sourceNotes: Börek encompasses a large family of filo pastry preparations eaten across Turkey, the Balkans, the Middle East, and Central Asia, originating in the Ottoman Empire where they were produced in the imperial court kitchen and spread throughout the empire. The most basic form is a filling of white cheese (beyaz peynir) and parsley enclosed in layers of filo brushed with butter or oil and baked; spinach is a common addition. Regional variations are vast: sigara böreği (cigarette-shaped rolls fried in oil), su böreği (water börek, a layered boiled filo version), and pul böreği (flaky pastry version) are just some of the forms. The recipe here is a standard oven-baked roll böreği that is simple to make at home.

content.text: Work quickly with filo pastry and keep unused sheets under a damp cloth at all times. The filling must not be too wet or it will seep through the pastry; squeeze the spinach very dry. Brush each sheet generously with butter; too little and the börek will be dry and papery.

items.preparation: wilted and squeezed completely dry; finely chopped
1 beaten into the filling; 1 beaten with 2 tbsp milk for brushing

content.text: Heat the oven to 190°C / fan 170°C / gas 5. Mix the spinach, feta, parsley, spring onion, one beaten egg, nutmeg, and pepper. Taste and add salt only if needed; feta is already salty.

Lay one sheet of filo on your work surface and brush generously with melted butter. Lay a second sheet on top and brush again. Spoon a line of filling along one long edge, leaving a 3 cm border on each short end. Roll up tightly from the filled edge into a log, tucking in the ends as you go. Repeat with the remaining filo and filling. Arrange on a baking tray.
Brush all over with the egg and milk mixture. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until deep golden and very crisp. Slice on the diagonal and serve warm.
